title: Enchiladas Rojas
subtitle: Corn tortillas filled with chicken and baked in a red chilli sauce
excerpt: Enchiladas rojas are corn tortillas filled with shredded chicken, rolled, and baked in a red sauce made from ancho and guajillo chillies. The corn tortillas are briefly dipped in the hot chilli sauce before filling to soften them and coat them in flavour. Topped with crumbled cheese and soured cream.
sourceNotes: Enchiladas (literally 'chillied') are a pre-Columbian Mexican preparation: corn tortillas dipped in chilli sauce. The Aztecs prepared versions of this dish. The filled, baked form common today is widespread throughout Mexico, with regional variations in the chilli sauce used. Ancho and guajillo together form the classic red sauce base.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble but don't bake, freeze tightly covered. Bake from frozen at 180°C for 35 to 40 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: The chilli sauce scales directly and keeps in the fridge for 5 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce and filling can both be made 2 days ahead.

content.text: The chilli sauce requires rehydrating dried chillies: toast them briefly in a dry pan, cover with boiling water, and soak for 20 minutes until soft. Do not skip the tortilla-dipping step: dipping each tortilla in the warm sauce before rolling adds flavour and prevents the tortillas cracking.

items.prepNote: grated, or use a mixture of cheddar and mozzarella

content.text: Toast the ancho and guajillo chillies in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute per side until they begin to blister and smell fragrant. Cover with boiling water and soak for 20 minutes until soft.

Drain the chillies, reserving the soaking water. Blend the chillies with the tinned tomatoes, garlic, onion, cumin, and oregano. Add a ladleful of the soaking water to thin if needed. Blend until smooth.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Pour in the blended sauce (it will spit). Fry, stirring, for 5 minutes until the sauce darkens and thickens. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Spread a ladle of sauce over the base of a roasting tin. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a frying pan. Briefly fry each corn tortilla for 10 seconds per side to warm it, then dip it quickly in the warm chilli sauce to coat.

Place 2 tablespoons of shredded chicken in the centre of each tortilla. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the roasting tin. Repeat with all tortillas. Pour the remaining sauce over. Scatter with grated cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes until the cheese is melted and the sauce is bubbling. Serve with the garnishes of your choice: soured cream, sliced jalapeños, coriander, diced onion.

items.symptom: Corn tortillas split and fall apart when rolling
items.cause: Tortillas were cold and dry, or not heated before rolling
items.fix: Corn tortillas must be warmed before rolling. Either heat briefly in the dry pan or wrap a stack in damp kitchen paper and microwave for 30 seconds.
